Classic Potato and Cheese Pierogi

Served at: Christmas Eve

Makes about 30-40 pierogi (Serves 6-8)Prep 1 hour 30 minCook 30 min

Pierogi are beloved Polish dumplings, and on Christmas Eve (Wigilia), they are a cherished part of the traditional meatless feast. These potato and cheese pierogi offer a comforting, savory bite, symbolizing warmth and family gathering during the holiday season.

Ingredients

  • For the Dough:
  • 2 1/2 cups (300g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1 large egg
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) warm water (or milk for a richer dough)
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 tablespoon (15g) unsalted butter, melted (or neutral oil)
  • For the Filling:
  • 1 1/2 pounds (680g) russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
  • 1 cup (113g) farmer's cheese or sharp cheddar cheese, crumbled or shredded
  • 1/4 cup (57g) unsalted butter
  • 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt, or to taste
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, or to taste
  • For Serving (Optional):
  • 1/4 cup (57g) unsalted butter
  • 1 medium onion, thinly sliced
  • Sour cream, for serving

Method

  1. Prepare the Filling: Place the peeled and quartered potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water, and add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
  2. While potatoes cook, melt 1/4 cup (57g) butter in a small skillet over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Set aside.
  3. Mash the drained potatoes thoroughly until smooth. Add the farmer's cheese (or cheddar), sautéed onion, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Mix well to combine. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Let the filling cool completely.
  4. Prepare the Dough: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour and salt. In a separate small bowl, whisk the egg, warm water (or milk), and melted butter.
  5. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 5-7 minutes, until smooth and elastic. Do not over-knead.
  6. Form the dough into a ball, lightly grease with oil, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rest at room temperature for at least 30 minutes (or up to 1 hour). This allows the gluten to relax, making the dough easier to roll.
  7. Assemble the Pierogi: Divide the dough into two or three portions. On a lightly floured surface, roll out one portion of dough very thinly, about 1/16 inch (1.5mm) thick. Use a 2.5-3 inch (6-7.5 cm) round cookie cutter or a glass to cut out circles.
  8. Place about 1 teaspoon of the cooled potato and cheese filling in the center of each dough circle. Fold the dough over the filling to create a half-moon shape. Pinch the edges firmly to seal, ensuring no filling leaks out. You can crimp the edges with a fork for extra security and a decorative touch.
  9. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling. If you have dough scraps, re-roll them once or twice.
  10. Cook the Pierogi: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Carefully drop the pierogi into the boiling water, a few at a time, making sure not to overcrowd the pot. They will sink to the bottom and then float to the top.
  11. Once the pierogi float, cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, or until the dough is tender. Remove with a slotted spoon and place them on a lightly oiled plate or baking sheet to prevent sticking.
  12. For Serving (Optional Frying): In a large skillet, melt 1/4 cup (57g) butter over medium heat. Add the thinly sliced onion and sauté until golden brown and caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
  13. Add the boiled pierogi to the skillet with the onions and cook for 2-3 minutes per side, until lightly golden and slightly crispy. Serve hot with a dollop of sour cream and the caramelized onions.

Tips

  • Make Ahead: Pierogi can be made ahead and frozen. After boiling, let them cool completely, then arrange in a single layer on a baking sheet and freeze. Once solid, transfer to a freezer-safe bag for up to 3 months. Cook from frozen by boiling or pan-frying.
  • Dough Consistency: If your dough is too sticky, add a little more flour; if too dry, add a tiny bit more warm water. The dough should be pliable and not stick to your hands.
  • Filling Variations: For Christmas Eve, a traditional meatless filling often includes sauerkraut and mushrooms. You can also add a pinch of nutmeg to the potato filling for extra flavor.
